entities.summary: The In Flanders Fields Museum is a museum in Ypres (Ieper), Belgium, dedicated to the study of the First World War. It occupies the second floor of the Cloth Hall (Lakenhalle) on the market square in the city centre. The building was largely destroyed by artillery during the war, but was afterwards reconstructed. In 1998 the original Ypres Salient Memorial Museum was refurbished and renamed In Flanders Fields Museum after the famous poem by Canadian John McCrae. Following a period of closure, the museum reopened on 11 June 2012. The curator, Piet Chielens, is a World War I historian. In Flanders Fields Museum is a museum in Europe, established in 1998. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The In Flanders Fields Museum played a significant role in preserving and promoting the history of World War I, with over 1 million visitors annually. Its efforts have contributed to a greater understanding of the war's impact on Belgium and Europe.
